executiveSummary: The OT/ICS threat landscape is at a critical posture this cycle due to simultaneous, actively exploited edge-access vectors and direct activity against industrial control assets. Multiple government advisories confirm ongoing intrusions against exposed PLCs in the U.S. water sector and opportunistic HMI compromises via VNC, alongside active exploitation of RMM and VPN/remote-access platforms used to bridge into OT environments. Supply-chain attacks targeting developer ecosystems raise risks to CI/CD pipelines supporting industrial operations. Direct OT device targeting: Threat actors are changing passwords/IPs on internet-exposed PLCs in Water/Wastewater, causing operational disruptions and manual mode operations. Immediate removal from the public internet and gateway-mediated access are mandated. Security Advisory Opportunistic HMI compromise via exposed VNC: Pro-Russia hacktivists continue mass scanning/brute forcing VNC to deface/change setpoints and suppress alarms on HMIs in Water, Food/Agriculture, and Energy sectors. Security Advisory Perimeter/RMM exploitation enabling OT pivots: Authentication bypass in N-able N-central is under active exploitation (new hotfix available); CISA added it to KEV. Hard-coded credential exposure in Cisco FMC is also being exploited. Restrict exposure, patch, and hunt for signs of misuse. CISA KEV View Article FortiGate credential leakage ("FortiBleed") at scale: Valid admin/VPN secrets observed in the wild; organizations must rotate credentials, enforce PBKDF2 hashing, and re-assess trusted tunnels (including site-to-site IPsec paths into OT). Security Advisory OT protocol/library risks: Unpatched protocol-integrity weakness across Mitsubishi Electric CC-Link IE TSN devices permits on-segment data tampering/DoS; MZ Automation's libiec61850 flaws (MMS/IEC 61850) carry DoS risks to substation operations-inventory and patch paths are priority. CISA Advisory CISA Advisory EVSE exposure: Multiple critical EV charger flaws (EVbee DC-80) enable unauthenticated remote control/RCE via OCPP/WebSockets-segment EVSE networks and enforce mTLS. CISA Bulletin Developer ecosystem supply-chain compromise: Active npm/Open VSX poisoning (Keyv-linked worm and "evil twin" extensions) steals tokens and propagates via trusted workflows, threatening CI/CD supporting industrial vendors/operators. Treat exposed runners/workstations as compromised and rotate all secrets. Supporting Report Supporting Report Nation-state infrastructure abuse continues: China-nexus actors leverage vast SOHO/IoT proxy botnets to mask operations and pre-position near critical infrastructure; edge device hygiene and segmentation remain urgent. Security Advisory

keyFindings.title: Active OT asset targeting (PLCs, exposed HMIs) is causing real operational impact; immediate internet exposure removal and access control are required
Edge/RMM compromises (N-able N-central, Cisco FMC) present rapid enterprise takeover and likely OT pivot paths via remote access jump hosts
FortiGate credential leaks at scale enable trusted-tunnel abuse into CI environments; credential and key rotation with PBKDF2 enforcement is urgent
OT communications and EV charging ecosystems expose protocol/library and controller weaknesses (CC-Link IE TSN, libiec61850, EVbee), risking process disruption if not segmented and patched

Active supply-chain compromises in developer toolchains (npm, Open VSX) threaten CI/CD and downstream ICS software integrity; organizations must harden provenance, disable install scripts in CI, and rotate credentials broadly

events.title: WWS: Internet-Exposed PLCs Under Active Attack
events.text: Actors are changing passwords/IPs on exposed PLCs, disrupting operations and requiring manual control. Remove exposure, enforce VPN/MFA, and restore from known-good backups.

events.title: Pro-Russia Hacktivists Exploit Exposed VNC on HMIs
events.text: Opportunistic attacks deface HMIs, change setpoints, suppress alarms, and lock out operators. Remove exposed VNC, harden accounts, and monitor 5900-5910.

events.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass (KEV) - Actively Exploited
events.text: Active exploitation enables account takeover and mass deployment. Patch immediately, restrict exposure, enforce MFA, and hunt for unauthorized jobs and tokens.

events.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Password (KEV)
events.text: Active exploitation of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center can yield full control over managed firewalls-patch, restrict access, audit changes, and validate integrity.

events.title: F5 BIG-IP APM iControl REST RCE - In the Wild
events.text: Confirmed exploitation with concrete IoCs. Remove public exposure, patch or hotfix, conduct compromise assessment, rotate credentials, and reimage if modified.

events.title: FortiBleed - FortiGate Credential Leaks at Scale
events.text: Leaked credentials facilitate AD harvesting and lateral movement via trusted tunnels. Rotate creds/keys, enforce PBKDF2, restrict admin access, and review logs/IoCs.

events.title: Mitsubishi Electric CC-Link IE TSN Protocol Integrity Flaw
events.text: On-segment attackers can tamper with control I/O or induce DoS. Enforce strict L2 segmentation, MACsec/ACLs, time-sync hardening, and ICS-aware monitoring.

events.title: China-Nexus Covert SOHO/IoT Proxy Networks
events.text: Large covert networks route operations and mask attribution; harden/replace edge devices, enforce egress controls, and segment OT with monitored jump hosts.

events.title: Ivanti EPMM Unauth RCE - Active Exploitation with PoC
events.text: Active exploitation with Ivanti-provided detection scripts. Isolate EPMM/Sentry, patch, review logs and internal pivots, rotate creds/tokens, and rebuild if compromised.

events.title: npm Supply-Chain Worm (Keyv-linked) - Credential Theft & Propagation
events.text: Preinstall hooks and editor integrations steal secrets and auto-publish. Disable scripts in CI, rotate tokens, isolate runners, and verify package provenance.

events.title: Open VSX "Evil Twin" Extensions Exfiltrate Developer Data
events.text: Malicious look-alike extensions exfiltrate developer/CI data. Enforce extension allowlists, block egress to indicators, and remove flagged IDs from fleets.

events.title: Zimbra 0-day Campaign (LAUNDRY BEAR) - Data Theft & Persistence
events.text: Phishing + XSS on message view enabled automated exfiltration and IMAP persistence. Patch ZCS, revoke app passcodes/2FA scratch keys, and hunt SOAP patterns.

events.title: IEC 61850 libiec61850 DoS Risks (Energy/Substations)
events.text: Potential DoS via malformed MMS on devices embedding the library; segment and restrict TCP/102 to authorized hosts only.

events.title: EV Chargers & Middleware (Multiple CVEs across weeks)
events.text: Multiple EVSE/OCPP and integration-stack exposures (ActiveMQ, IoTDB, NiFi, DAQFactory) across CISA weekly bulletins.

events.title: GeoServer RCE - FCEB IR Lessons (transferable controls)
events.text: Real-world multi-host compromise via GeoServer; adopt egress filtering, disable risky DB features, and hunt for web shells/BITS misuse.

events.title: Check Point Security Mgmt Server Auth Bypass (Hotfixes)
events.text: Critical flaw allows full takeover of firewall policy management (no public exploitation noted in article). Apply latest jumbo takes and restrict access.

descriptions: Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190): N-central auth-bypass; F5 iControl REST RCE; GeoServer RCE; EVSE/OCPP endpoints.
Valid Accounts (T1078) and Credential Access (T1003/T1555): FortiBleed credential use; AD/NTLM/2FA token theft in multiple campaigns.
Remote Services (T1021): RDP/SSH, exposed VNC to HMIs (loss of view/control).
Lateral Movement via Remote Admin (T1021.004/T1570): RMM abuse, PsExec/PAExec; partner VPN trust abuse.
Command and Control via Proxy/Covert Channels (T1090/T1572): Residential/SOHO proxy botnets; WebSocket/DNS exfil.
Defense Evasion via DLL Sideloading (T1574.002) and Living-off-the-Land: OctLurk/SilkLurk, GeoServer/SQL xp_cmdshell, BITS jobs.
Supply-Chain Compromise (T1195): npm/Open VSX poisoning; AI-agent assisted PR backdoors.

outlook72h: Expect continued opportunistic exploitation of exposed PLCs/VNC and accelerated targeting of unpatched RMM/VPN/edge consoles listed in KEV. High likelihood of follow-on activity abusing leaked FortiGate credentials for trusted VPN ingress; monitor and re-establish trust boundaries. Developer-ecosystem threats likely persist (npm/Open VSX); anticipate refreshed indicators and copycats-keep revocation and response procedures active. OT protocol/library issues (CC-Link IE TSN, IEC 61850) remain latent risk; prioritize compensating controls while coordinating with vendors for updates.
